text:
Maya: Heads-up — noticed a short spike of invalid SSO assertions followed by a wave of MFA prompts across multiple orgs. A subset of sessions show immediate revokes. Could be MFA fatigue or a probe against service accounts. @here :eyes:

incident-bot: Detection: sso.anomaly.alert — 82 events in 4m; anomaly_score=0.92; affected_tenants=3

Josh: Can you paste a quick log sample and affected client IPs? I'll spin up temporary deny rules if this is still active.

Maya: Log snippet (redacted):
```
time=2026-03-18T16:12:34Z event=assertion_failure tenant=acme-corp user=svc-deploy-agent ua=python-requests/2.28 ip=185.87.45.23 geo=BG
time=2026-03-18T16:12:36Z event=mfa_push_sent tenant=acme-corp user=user@acme-corp ua=ios/17.3 ip=34.201.5.12 geo=US
time=2026-03-18T16:12:40Z event=session_revoke tenant=acme-corp session_id=sess_8d3f ip=185.87.45.23
```
Two tenants show same source ASN and a mix of impossible travel patterns (BG -> US within seconds).

Lina: Claire, any support tickets about lockouts? Claire: Yep — about a dozen users reported multiple MFA prompts and at least 2 manual password resets initiated. They were temporarily blocked by our auto-lock policy.

Aaron: Recommend immediate containment steps: 1) Add 185.87.45.0/24 to denylist at WAF level; 2) revoke refresh tokens for affected tenants via IdP API; 3) disable non-interactive SSO for service accounts until we validate keys. I can run the IdP calls.

Josh: I'm for quick network-level blocks + token revokes. Also set a short-lived override to require reauth for all admins in affected tenants.

Maya: Also seeing a handful of service-account key rotations around the same time — could be credential stuffing against CI credentials. Can we confirm any KMS accesses?

DevOps-bot: KMS access log excerpt (filtered):
```
2026-03-18T16:11:59Z principal=svc-ci-runner key=projects/redwood/keys/deploy-kms action=decrypt status=OK ip=54.36.12.7
2026-03-18T16:12:05Z principal=svc-ci-runner key=projects/redwood/keys/deploy-kms action=decrypt status=OK ip=185.87.45.23
```
The second line timestamp aligns with SSO anomalies.

Lina: If the same service principal is used from both US and BG IPs, we should treat as compromised. Action: rotate the KMS envelope keys for deploy-kms and rotate the service account keys. Aaron — can you coordinate with infra to rotate and rotate access tokens? Note: KMS rotation has downstream deployment implications; schedule a canary first.

Aaron: Will do emergency rotation for the one service account in a scoped rollout — will not rotate global tenant keys yet. I'll also add RBAC restriction: temporary deny of 'project:iam.serviceAccounts.actAs' for the compromised principal.

Claire: I'll prepare a short user comms template for affected tenants (explain lockouts, advise credential rotation, contact support).

Josh: Forensics checklist — capture full IdP assertion payloads, full KMS audit log range 15m before/after, and list of active refresh tokens for the affected tenants. I'll snapshot the relevant logs to the secure evidence bucket (read-only).

Maya: Quick note on mitigations: enable step-up on risky geos and rate-limit MFA pushes per user to prevent fatigue attacks. Also add an alert rule for service-account decrypts from atypical ASN.

Lina: Post-incident actions: 1) Confirm root cause (compromised CI secret vs SSO replay); 2) Add detection for simultaneous assert_fail + decrypt events; 3) Document RBAC change and revert window; 4) Run tabletop next week. Assign owners?

Maya: I'll own detection tuning and the alert. Aaron owns KMS/service-account rotation. Claire owns tenant comms. Josh owns forensics bundle. Lina will track postmortem and next steps.

Aaron: Starting rotation now — scoping to svc-ci-runner only. Blocking 185.87.45.0/24 at edge.

incident-bot: Incident created — INC-2026-0318-42; severity=medium; owners=[Maya,Aaron,Josh,Claire,Lina]

Claire: Sending comms draft to Lina/Maya for review.

Maya: Thanks — small wins: blocks in place, tokens revoked, KMS rotation started. Keep channel updated with any user-facing impacts. :thumbsup:
